newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends firmer, but trapped in range.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends firmer, but trapped in range.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures ended firmer Tuesday, as speculative short covering and bargain hunting from manufacturers lifted the market off recent lows.
But the market encountered fairly solid resistance toward the highs, capping the day's advance well below key chart resistance levels, traders said.
Nearby December rose $9 a tonne, to $1,356, having ranged from $1,350 to $1,366. Second-position March, which benefitted from keen speculative selling on the nearby switch, rose $14, to $1,388.
Volume on the day reached a steady 9,089 lots.
With producers eager to lock in prices toward the $1,400 mark, and good buying from processors at the lows, dealers said the market may stay confined to a narrow range for the time being.

"We're very much in this $1,350-1,400 trading range basis December," said one trader. "Ivory Coast has sold some major tonnage into the rallies over the past few weeks, and the industry is buying scale-down."
Technically, today's performance solidified $1,350 as a support level basis December, while a major upside target loomed at $1,378-1,382, a chart gap created last week.
-- Wendy Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640
